# Ingestion-to-Case Requirements Checklist: Medicine Change Ingestion-to-Case Pipeline

**Purpose**: Review the completeness, clarity, consistency, and testability of the ingestion-to-case requirements
**Created**: 2026-10-06
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 - Are the specific Fimea Basic Register files and medicine categories in scope identified, or is the dependency on deciding them before implementation explicit? [Completeness, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK002 - Are the catalog fields that count as a relevant change enumerated or assigned to a named decision gate before change detection can be implemented? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004, §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK003 - Are source release identity, source chronology evidence, local retrieval time, and raw-file provenance requirements separately defined? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK004 - Are the pharmacist's required access and role assumptions defined for the open-case view, or explicitly deferred? [Gap, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK005 - Are the expected display boundaries for simulated medication records clear enough to avoid unnecessary personal data, even when the data is fictional? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013, §FR-010]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK006 - Is “source update information” clearly distinguished from retrieval time and sufficient to determine which releases may be compared? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK007 - Is “relevant medicine-information change” bounded to catalog fields and clearly distinguished from clinical significance or clinical-content changes? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK008 - Are the matching identifier and granularity (authorization versus package) specified consistently for source records and simulated medication records? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK009 - Are the terms “open review case,” “NEW,” and “important status transition” defined consistently, including the creation event? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007, §FR-010, §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK010 - Are “verified,” “inferred,” “unknown,” and “conflicting” information defined with decision criteria for assigning each classification? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK011 - Do source snapshot, detected-change, case, and status-event requirements all preserve an unbroken trace to the original source evidence? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002, §FR-005, §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK012 - Are the rules for unknown/conflicting release order consistent with the requirement to detect changes and the prohibition on presenting unsupported changes as verified? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK013 - Are the pharmacist view's read-only boundary and human-review responsibility consistent with the prohibition on autonomous status changes and automatic case closure? [Consistency, Spec §FR-010, §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK014 - Are the stated feature exclusions consistent across the functional requirements, assumptions, and project constitution? [Consistency, Spec §FR-016]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK015 - Is the acceptance dataset's size, composition, and coverage defined so the “every” and “exactly one” outcomes can be objectively evaluated? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001, §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK016 - Are the success criteria for source traceability and evidence classification objectively assessable for every created case? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003, §FR-011, §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK017 - Do success criteria explicitly cover failed/partial ingestion, unknown source chronology, and ambiguous matching outcomes? [Coverage, Spec §SC-001–SC-006, §FR-015]

## Scenario and Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK018 - Are baseline behavior, repeated ingestion, missing source data, malformed records, unavailable evidence, and no-match/ambiguous-match outcomes specified without conflicting interpretations? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-008–FR-009, §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK019 - Are recovery expectations defined after a failed or partial scheduled ingestion, including whether and how a later complete release can be processed safely? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK020 - Are source-release publication cadence and polling expectations stated so the schedule does not imply data freshness beyond Fimea's release availability? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001, §Assumptions]

## Non-Functional Requirements and Dependencies

- [ ] CHK021 - Are acceptable processing duration and operational visibility requirements specified for a scheduled release, or explicitly left without a target for the prototype? [Completeness, Spec §SC-001, Plan §Technical Context]
- [ ] CHK022 - Are source access, automation/reuse permissions, current file schema, and release-order evidence recorded as prerequisites with a clear owner or decision point? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions, Plan §Research Plan and Decisions]
- [ ] CHK023 - Are privacy and safety requirements explicit for source fixtures, simulated records, logs, demonstrations, and stored evidence—not only the visible case data? [Coverage, Spec §FR-013, §FR-014]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK024 - Is it clear whether an ordered catalog difference is only an information change for pharmacist review and never an implicit indication of clinical risk or urgency? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-004, §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK025 - Are all unresolved choices—source files, relevant fields, matching key/granularity, and acceptance dataset—tracked as decisions that must be resolved before dependent implementation tasks begin? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]

## Notes

- This checklist evaluates requirements quality only; it does not verify implementation behavior.
- Leave all items unchecked until a reviewer evaluates the requirement wording and records findings.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
